Hi Morgan — great to sync. Attaching a short playbook and a topology PNG to make the sandbox ticket easier for your infra team. High level checklist below; full playbook attached (redwood_network_playbook_v1.pdf).

Quick validation checklist (minimal):
- VPC: 10.150.0.0/16 (single private subnet for inference nodes)
- Subnet egress: allow outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDNs/IP ranges (for control plane):
  - control.redwood.ai (TLS 443)
  - telemetry.redwood.ai (TLS 443)
- Firewall: allow inbound from your admin bastion IP only to SSH (22) on the GPU node for the window
- KMS: provide key ARN; we will request a test wrap/unwrap during validation
- DNS: ensure private DNS can resolve control.redwood.ai within the VPC
- NTP: allow UDP 123 to pool.ntp.org or your internal NTP servers

Temporary ACLs we request you open for the window:
- Outbound 443 to control.redwood.ai and telemetry.redwood.ai
- Outbound 443 to packages.redwood.ai (for agent bootstrap)

I’m copying Dev and Marcus for the low-level VPN/MTU and node bootstrap steps. Proposed validation runbook: Thu Oct 3 — pre-checks; Fri Oct 4 — validation tests; Fri Oct 5 — post-check and sign-off. If that schedule works, we’ll send a short mutual action plan (MAP).

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

Morgan / Evelyn — quick technical notes to avoid surprises during bootstrap: 

1) VPN MTU: our agent uses GRPC over TLS and is sensitive to fragmentation. Recommend MTU 1400 on the VPN tunnel. If you have an intermediate firewall, set MSS clamp to 1380.

2) IP allowlist: the playbook lists FQDNs; if you prefer IPs for ticketing, we can provide a short-lived CIDR list for the window. Note: we fail over to alternate control nodes in a different AZ, so please allow both AZ ranges if you pick IPs.

3) KMS tests: we will perform a test encrypt/decrypt roundtrip using a single test object. Please create a role with kms:Encrypt kms:Decrypt permissions scoped to the test key.

4) Bootstrapping: the node will reach out to packages.redwood.ai to download the agent binary. If your egress policy restricts domains, allow that FQDN.

If you want, I can paste a short iptables-friendly command collection for your infra engineers to run as pre-checks.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
